cards.title: Childhood Sexual Abuse: Supporting Family Victims
cards.body: When a family member discloses abuse, prioritize making them feel safe and heard. Assess any ongoing danger the perpetrator poses to younger family members and seek professional guidance.

cards.title: When Praise Backfires: Children and Pressure
cards.body: Some children experience praise as pressure rather than support, asking parents to stop complimenting them. Understanding this reaction helps parents adjust their encouragement style.

cards.title: The Trouble With Time-Outs as Discipline
cards.body: Time-outs are popular discipline strategies but often fail in practice. Understanding why can help parents choose more effective behavioral approaches.

cards.title: Parallel Parenting vs. Co-Parenting After Divorce
cards.body: Divorced parents often share less information as their estrangement grows. However, critical information sharing remains essential for children's wellbeing.

cards.title: Narcissistic Parenting: Recovering From 'Not Good Enough'
cards.body: Children raised feeling inadequate by narcissistic parents can recover with the right support. New research reveals paths to healing and building healthier self-worth.

cards.title: Screen-Free Childhoods Are Increasingly Rare
cards.body: Today's children have never known a world without screens. Protecting time for reading, play, and human connection from birth is more critical than ever.

cards.title: Yoga Supports Eating Disorder Recovery in Youth
cards.body: Yoga can aid eating disorder recovery by promoting body acceptance and self-compassion. A mindful approach helps teens rebuild a healthier connection with their bodies.

cards.title: Empty Nest: Parenting Through Major Life Transitions
cards.body: When adult children leave for university, parents face unexpected emotional challenges. Acknowledging the difficulty of 'empty nesting' helps families navigate this major life change.

cards.title: Family Festivals: Why Kids Belong at Music Events
cards.body: Families with children enrich festival experiences rather than diminish them. Including toddlers and young children adds joy and magic to community celebrations.
